newsitem.title: ITALY: British drugs case teenager to be freed in Italy.
newsitem.headline: British drugs case teenager to be freed in Italy.

text.p: An Italian court on Monday gave British teenager Melanie Jackman a three-year suspended sentence for heroin smuggling.
"She was given three years, suspended, and will be out tomorrow," a British embassy official said.

Jackman, 19, from Brighton, was detained near Naples in June last year with British teenager Marianne Platt, who is on probation and whose case was heard separately because she was a minor at the time of her arrest.
Police found four kg (nine lbs) of heroin in a hidden compartment of a holdall they were carrying. The girls had arrived at Rome's Fiumicino airport on a flight from Istanbul.

Both girls have said they did not know they were carrying drugs. Jackman's parents have been quoted as saying Melanie told them she thought she was bringing money to Italy for a man she had befriended on Brighton pier in southern England.
